params.script_inline:
import sys, json, uuid, datetime, math

# The cell that turns a decision into a change -- and the cell that refuses one.
#
# Everything the judge said is re-checked here, deterministically, because a
# model in a control loop is safe exactly to the degree that its output is
# checked by something that cannot be talked round:
#
#   * the RADIUS  -- model choice, numeric params and, since GH #927, text
#     slots of the classes the charter lists. A topology change is downgraded
#     to a proposal, never executed; so is a text only its owner may change,
#     and a text that is the colony's identity is not even that.
#   * the REVERT PLAN -- present, well formed, and actually the inverse of the
#     change. A cycle without one is invalid by charter rule.
#   * the EVIDENCE -- a text change is applied only on a validation batch that
#     says it works (GH #927). A model or a number is measured after the fact;
#     a sentence the colony reads is judged BEFORE it lands, because a better
#     metric on ten conversations is a coin toss with a receipt.
#   * the LANE -- the change goes out as an ordinary params update, or for a
#     text slot as a `slot_update`, addressed to the one cell it names. There
#     is no operator lane here and there must not be: a control loop that can
#     override the gates it runs under is not governed, it is merely polite.
#
# GH #304: it used to leave as a `swap_nodes` diff, which was wrong twice over.
# The validator requires `match.name` and `with` on every entry and reads no
# `params` beside the name, so nothing this cell emitted was ever applied -- in
# either direction. And `swap_nodes` could not have carried it anyway: the spec
# defines it as an edge swing, which stages a fresh cell and re-points the
# edges, never an in-place rewrite of a running cell's config. What the radius
# actually describes is a params update, so that is what goes out.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
# This cell's OWN configuration arrives on the same stdin document: `params` is
# one of its three top-level objects, beside `envelope` and `body`, and the
# substrate always sets it ({} when there is nothing to hand over). Every knob
# below is read from it, so each one is per-INSTANCE configuration -- two argus
# instances of one colony step at speeds of their own, and a mutation retunes
# one of them without touching a colony-wide environment (GH #138). The literal
# beside each name is the shipped default; it is the same value the template
# config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three against each
# other.
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to null is "not configured", not a crash: an
    # operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    # A blank string falls back as well -- there is no number in it to read.
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _list(key, default):
    """A declared key set. The ruling writes it as a JSON array; a comma string
    is read the same way, because `override_params` reaches this knob as a
    config line somebody types and the shipped default used to be one. Anything
    else is EMPTY rather than half-read -- a radius that lost half its keys
    would refuse changes nobody said it may not make.
    """
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        v = v.split(",")
    if not isinstance(v, list):
        return []
    return [str(n).strip() for n in v if str(n).strip()]


MAX_STEP_PCT = _int("max_numeric_step_pct", 50)

# The numeric half of the radius, as a set of KEYS rather than a set of cells.
#
# This cell sees a path and a key and nothing else -- it cannot look up what
# type of cell sits at a target, and there is no lane through which it could.
# But whether an overlay lands is a fact about the cell TYPE: a params update is
# merged by the types that have a params lane (`llm`, `store`, `timer`, `mcp`,
# `proxy`, `subcolony`, `harness`) and by nobody else. A `code` cell has no such
# lane at all -- it would take the body as an ordinary input and run its script
# on it.
#
# So the radius is expressed the one way this cell can check honestly: the keys
# it will act on are the ones the `llm` params lane accepts at runtime, which is
# the cell type the radius is actually about (model choice first). A cap like
# `max_iter` lives on a `code` cell, and sending an overlay for it would produce
# a receipt saying `applied` over a colony where nothing moved -- which is the
# GH #304 defect class a second time, on the other half of the radius.
#
# An operator who has wired a target that CAN receive another key widens this,
# and the widening is a declaration rather than a hope: the receipt for a key
# outside the set names the key it refused. Since GH #138 the widening is per
# INSTANCE -- one argus may watch a colony whose radius is wider than another's.
NUMERIC_PARAM_KEYS = _list("numeric_param_keys", ["temperature",
                                                  "max_tokens",
                                                  "external_timeout_ms",
                                                  "attachment_timeout_ms"])


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(
        "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def emit(route, phase, body=None, extra=None):
    # `carry` is ALWAYS present, empty where it means nothing (GH #927). The
    # edge to ./receipts lifts `hop.carry` into the context, and an edge
    # modifier reading a key that is not there is a CEL error that skips the
    # edge -- so a receipt without it would never reach the store. Same rule
    # the meter's `emit()` keeps for its own keys (GH #462).
    h = {"route": route, "phase": phase, "cycle_id": "", "outcome": "",
         "carry": ""}
    h.update(extra or {})
    m = {"header": h}
    m.update(body or {})
    return m


def receipt(operation, phase="written", carry=None, **rest):
    # `phase` and `carry` ride to ./receipts and come back in the context of
    # its answer. Every write goes out as `written`, which the echo branch
    # drops; the one read this cell resumes on (`evalwait`, GH #927) names its
    # own phase and carries the verdict it was asked for.
    args = {"operation": operation}
    args.update(rest)
    return emit("rstore", phase, {
        "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                      "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], "text": json.dumps(args)}]},
        {"carry": json.dumps(carry) if carry is not None else ""})


def as_obj(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v
    if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
        try:
            p = json.loads(v)
        except Exception:
            return {}
        return p if isinstance(p, dict) else {}
    return {}


def as_list(v):
    # The judge hop's context carries lists as JSON text (`ar_rules`,
    # `ar_hints`), the meter's revert order as a list. Anything unreadable is
    # EMPTY -- which for the rules means the closed defaults below, never "no
    # limits" (GH #927).
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return v
    if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
        try:
            p = json.loads(v)
        except Exception:
            return []
        return p if isinstance(p, list) else []
    return []


def rows_of(d):
    msgs = d.get("messages") or []
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        v = json.loads(msgs[-1].get("text") or "null")
    except Exception:
        return []
    return v if isinstance(v, list) else []


def numeric(v):
    try:
        f = float(v)
        return f
    except Exception:
        return None


def int_or(v, default):
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return default
    try:
        return int(v)
    except Exception:
        return default


# The charter's rules, as far as this cell reads them (GH #927). It used to
# read none: the radius was the kinds wired into `in_radius` plus a key set.
# The text half of the radius is charter DATA instead -- which classes exist,
# which are the owner's, which are nobody's -- and it arrives on the judge hop
# (`ar_rules`), because the meter read the rules for the same cycle.
#
# Every default is the CLOSED one. A row that is missing or blank widens
# nothing: no `text_slots` in the radius, no slot class, the owner's classes
# and identity kept out -- so a rules list that failed to travel refuses every
# text change instead of admitting all of them.
DEFAULT_RADIUS = "model,numeric_params"
DEFAULT_EVAL_MIN_BATCH = "30"
DEFAULT_SLOT_CLASSES = ""
DEFAULT_OWNER_ONLY = "persona,behaviour"
DEFAULT_NEVER = "identity"

# The keys of an evaluator's verdict (README § 2.3, `in_eval`). Only these
# travel on: the verdict rides a hop value into the store read and back, and
# lands in `cycles.evidence` -- an evaluator that answered with its whole batch
# attached would put the batch there (review finding M8).
EVAL_KEYS = ("verdict", "batch_id", "n", "baseline", "candidate", "delta_pct")


def rule(rules, kind, default):
    """The value of the first rule row of `kind`, or `default`. A blank value
    is the default too: an operator who empties a row means "not configured",
    and not configured is closed."""
    for r in rules:
        if isinstance(r, dict) and str(r.get("kind") or "") == kind:
            v = r.get("value")
            return default if v is None or not str(v).strip() else str(v)
    return default


def rule_set(rules, kind, default_csv):
    """A rule whose value is a set: a comma list, trimmed, blanks dropped.

    A value of nothing but commas and blanks names no member, so it reads as
    a missing row -- the closed default -- and not as a set configured empty
    (review finding M7, ruling G.8): `never: ","` must not switch off the
    identity guard that `never: ""` keeps.
    """
    def split(v):
        return [p.strip() for p in v.split(",") if p.strip()]
    return split(rule(rules, kind, default_csv)) or split(default_csv)


def slot_class(change):
    """The class a text change names, trimmed and case-folded. `Identity` is
    identity: without the fold it passed the `never` check and came back as
    `key_outside_radius_Identity` -- refused, but for the wrong reason, and
    an owner-only `Persona` was refused instead of proposed (review finding
    M7)."""
    return str(change.get("class") or "").strip().lower()


def class_set(rules, kind, default_csv):
    """A class list of the charter, folded the way `slot_class` folds."""
    return [c.lower() for c in rule_set(rules, kind, default_csv)]


def in_radius(kind, key, rules=None):
    """Is this (kind, key) inside the radius? A reason code, or "" if it is.

    Its own function because BOTH directions have to ask it. A revert that is
    waved through a bound the change had to pass is not a way back, it is a
    second door -- and the receipt would say `reverted` over a colony still
    running the value the cycle failed to prove.

    GH #927: a text slot is the third kind, its key a slot name. Whether text
    slots are in the radius at all is the charter's `radius` row, asked here
    only when the caller HAS the rules. The decide path never reaches this
    with a text slot -- `classify_slot` asks the whole question (never, owner,
    radius, class) first -- so what is left for this function is the way back.
    """
    if kind not in ("model", "numeric_param", "text_slot"):
        return "outside_radius"
    if kind == "text_slot":
        if rules is not None and \
                "text_slots" not in rule_set(rules, "radius", DEFAULT_RADIUS):
            return "outside_radius"
        return "" if key else "slot_key_missing"
    if kind == "numeric_param" and not key:
        return "param_key_missing"
    if kind == "numeric_param" and key not in NUMERIC_PARAM_KEYS:
        # Refused, not applied. A cycle that cannot land is a recorded outcome
        # with the key in its reason code -- "we did not move it" and "we moved
        # it and it did nothing" must never read the same.
        #
        # The code says `key_outside_radius` and not `no_params_receiver`: this
        # cell cannot see a target's cell type, so it does not know whether a key
        # it refuses has a receiver somewhere. `system_max_slots` has one and is
        # immutable at runtime; `max_iter` has none at all. What is TRUE of both
        # is that they are outside the declared set, and that is what it says.
        return "key_outside_radius_" + key
    return ""


def check_change(change, rules=None):
    """The change-shaped half of the re-check. A reason code, or "".

    Its own function for the same reason `in_radius` is one, a bound further
    out: BOTH directions have to ask it. GH #326 -- the revert path ran the
    radius check alone, so a stored plan with no value, or with a target no
    edge can carry, left as a params update nobody merges under a receipt
    reading `reverted`.

    Order matters: absolute target first, then radius, because a change outside
    the radius must be refused whatever else is right about it.
    """
    target = str(change.get("target") or "")
    kind = str(change.get("kind") or "")
    key = str(change.get("key") or "")
    if not target.startswith("/"):
        return "target_not_absolute"
    reason = in_radius(kind, key, rules)
    if reason:
        return reason
    if change.get("to") in (None, ""):
        return "no_new_value"
    if kind == "text_slot" and not isinstance(change.get("to"), str):
        # A slot holds text; a number or an object is no text a cell can read.
        return "no_new_value"
    if kind == "numeric_param":
        old, new = numeric(change.get("from")), numeric(change.get("to"))
        if new is None:
            return "new_value_not_numeric"
        # A cap that jumps by an order of magnitude is not a tuning step, it is
        # a different colony. The step limit keeps one cycle's mistake small
        # enough that the next cycle can still measure its way out.
        #
        # Inert for a revert plan by construction: a plan carries no `from`, so
        # `old` is None and the step is never computed. The way back is a
        # restoration of a value this loop itself moved away from, and the size
        # of that move was already bounded on the way there.
        if old is not None and old != 0:
            step = abs(new - old) / abs(old) * 100.0
            if step > MAX_STEP_PCT:
                return "step_too_large_%.0f_pct" % step
    return ""


def check(change, plan, require_plan):
    """The deterministic re-check of a decision. A reason code, or "".

    The change-shaped half is `check_change`, which the revert path runs too.
    What is left here is the half that is about the PLAN, and only the decide
    path has one to check.

    The rules are an EMPTY list on purpose, which closes the text half of the
    radius on this path: a text slot is decided by `classify_slot` and applied
    only after an evaluation (GH #927). Were one ever routed here, it would be
    refused as `outside_radius`, never waved through on a model's checks.
    """
    reason = check_change(change, [])
    if reason:
        return reason
    if not require_plan:
        return ""
    target = str(change.get("target") or "")
    kind = str(change.get("kind") or "")
    key = str(change.get("key") or "")
    if not plan:
        return "no_revert_plan"
    if str(plan.get("target") or "") != target:
        return "revert_plan_wrong_target"
    if str(plan.get("kind") or "") != kind:
        return "revert_plan_wrong_kind"
    if kind == "numeric_param" and str(plan.get("key") or "") != key:
        return "revert_plan_wrong_key"
    if plan.get("to") in (None, ""):
        return "revert_plan_has_no_value"
    # The plan has to lead BACK. A "revert" to the value we are moving to is a
    # plan that changes nothing, and it would pass every structural check.
    if str(plan.get("to")) == str(change.get("to")):
        return "revert_plan_is_not_inverse"
    if change.get("from") not in (None, "") and \
            str(plan.get("to")) != str(change.get("from")):
        return "revert_plan_does_not_restore_the_original"
    return ""


def charter_gate(change, rules):
    """The classes the charter keeps from this loop: `[status, reason]` for a
    text in one of them, `[]` for any other.

    Its own function because the decide path asks it BEFORE it looks at the
    judge's `action` (review finding I3). Asked under `change` only, a
    `propose` carried an identity text into `cycles.change` as a proposal --
    the charter's `never` says not even that -- and an owner-only text closed
    as `judge_propose`, a row the owner is never pointed at, instead of as
    `owner_approval_required`.
    """
    cls = slot_class(change)
    if cls in class_set(rules, "never", DEFAULT_NEVER):
        return ["refused", "identity_out_of_radius"]
    if cls in class_set(rules, "owner_only", DEFAULT_OWNER_ONLY):
        return ["proposed", "owner_approval_required"]
    return []


def classify_slot(change, rules):
    """Which way a text change goes (GH #927): `[status, reason]`, the status
    one of `refused`, `proposed` or `eval`.

    The ORDER is the rule. Identity first, before the radius and before
    anything the judge argued, so no radius edit reaches it and it is not even
    a proposal. The owner's classes next: a proposal is a message to a human,
    and the radius bounds what this loop DOES, not what it may ask. Those two
    are `charter_gate`. Only then the radius and the class list, with the
    codes a kind and a numeric key outside the radius get (`outside_radius`,
    `key_outside_radius_<...>`), so a refusal reads the same on every half of
    the radius.
    """
    gate = charter_gate(change, rules)
    if gate:
        return gate
    cls = slot_class(change)
    if "text_slots" not in rule_set(rules, "radius", DEFAULT_RADIUS):
        return ["refused", "outside_radius"]
    if not cls:
        return ["refused", "slot_class_missing"]
    if cls not in class_set(rules, "slot_classes", DEFAULT_SLOT_CLASSES):
        return ["refused", "key_outside_radius_" + cls]
    return ["eval", ""]


def revert_ok_text(change, plan, require_plan):
    """The re-check of a text change and its way back (GH #927). A reason
    code, or "".

    `check()` for the text half, with one difference that matters: the plan
    has to restore the original BYTE FOR BYTE. `check()` compares through
    `str()`, which is right for a number (4096 and "4096" are one cap) and
    wrong for a text -- a trailing space, or a number where a sentence stood,
    is another text. A plan that restores something ALMOST like the original
    leads to a third text nobody evaluated, and a missing `from` is a plan
    nobody can check at all.
    """
    target = str(change.get("target") or "")
    key = str(change.get("key") or "")
    to = change.get("to")
    if not target.startswith("/"):
        return "target_not_absolute"
    if not key:
        return "slot_key_missing"
    if not isinstance(to, str) or not to:
        return "no_new_value"
    if not require_plan:
        return ""
    if not plan:
        return "no_revert_plan"
    if str(plan.get("target") or "") != target:
        return "revert_plan_wrong_target"
    if str(plan.get("kind") or "") != "text_slot":
        return "revert_plan_wrong_kind"
    if str(plan.get("key") or "") != key:
        return "revert_plan_wrong_key"
    back = plan.get("to")
    if back in (None, ""):
        return "revert_plan_has_no_value"
    if back == to:
        return "revert_plan_is_not_inverse"
    orig = change.get("from")
    if not (isinstance(back, str) and isinstance(orig, str) and back == orig):
        return "revert_plan_does_not_restore_the_original"
    return ""


def batch_min_of(rules, goal):
    """How large a validation batch a text change needs (GH #927): the LARGER
    of the charter's floor and the goal's own `min_samples`. A goal that will
    not act on a measurement of fewer than 45 samples does not act on a batch
    of 30 because the charter's floor happens to be lower."""
    floor = int_or(rule(rules, "eval_min_batch", DEFAULT_EVAL_MIN_BATCH),
                   int(DEFAULT_EVAL_MIN_BATCH))
    return max(floor, int_or(goal.get("min_samples"), 0))


def count_of(v):
    """A batch size as a whole number, or 0.

    Read the way `delta_pct` is read -- a number, or a text holding one -- so
    `40`, `40.0` and `"40"` are one batch of 40 (review finding M7: a count
    as text and an integral float read as 0 while a delta as text was taken).
    What is still no count: a fraction, a bool, NaN, infinity, anything else.
    """
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return 0
    f = numeric(v)
    if f is None or not math.isfinite(f) or not f.is_integer():
        return 0
    return int(f)


def evidence_ok(ev, goal, batch_min):
    """Does an evaluation batch license the change? `["apply", ""]` or
    `["discarded", reason]` (GH #927).

    The batch size is asked FIRST, before the verdict: a verdict on a batch
    below the floor is noise whichever way it points, and the receipt names
    what was actually wrong with it. `n` is read by `count_of`; no count reads
    as 0. The delta is read in the goal's own direction against the goal's own
    floor; a goal with no direction this cell knows (`observe`, or none at
    all) licenses nothing.
    """
    n = count_of(ev.get("n"))
    if n < batch_min:
        return ["discarded", "no_evidence_%d" % n]
    if str(ev.get("verdict") or "") != "pass":
        return ["discarded", "eval_failed"]
    raw = ev.get("delta_pct")
    delta = None if isinstance(raw, bool) else numeric(raw)
    floor = numeric(goal.get("min_delta_pct") or 0)
    if delta is None or floor is None or not math.isfinite(delta):
        return ["discarded", "below_delta"]
    direction = str(goal.get("direction") or "")
    if direction == "lower" and -delta >= floor:
        return ["apply", ""]
    if direction == "higher" and delta >= floor:
        return ["apply", ""]
    return ["discarded", "below_delta"]


def params_update_for(change):
    """The change as a params update for one cell.

    A model swap and a numeric param are the same shape at this level: both are
    a params update on one cell, which is what keeps radius v1 small enough to
    reason about.
    """
    target = str(change.get("target"))
    key = "model" if str(change.get("kind")) == "model" else str(change.get("key"))
    value = change.get("to")
    if str(change.get("kind")) == "numeric_param":
        n = numeric(value)
        value = int(n) if n is not None and float(n).is_integer() else n
    return {"target": target, "params": {key: value}}


def change_message(change, cid, outcome):
    """The wire a running cell already understands, addressed by hop.

    The body is a params update with an EMPTY `system` slot and no `messages`:
    the target merges the overlay into its live params, persists it in its own
    cell.db and emits nothing at all -- no inference, no provider call, no cost.
    The empty slot is not decoration; a body carrying none of `system`,
    `messages` or `attachments` is not a UBF body and never leaves the colony.
    The absent `messages[]` is the other half: a turn beside the overlay would
    buy an inference nobody asked for.

    `hop.target` names the cell, the way `llm-registry/hand` names a subscriber.
    An edge cannot be computed from a body, so the parent draws one per cell the
    loop may reach -- which makes the set of reachable cells a fact about the
    seed rather than about what the judge wrote down.

    A text slot has a wire of its own (GH #927): `slot_update`, body
    `{messages: [], slot: {name, text}}`, the same hop. A cell's text is not
    one of its params, so the overlay cannot carry it, and the parent draws
    the edges for it exactly as for `mutate`. `hop.cycle_id` matters on both
    wires: the probe finds the change at the target only by the cycle's id
    (`path_prefix_cycle_total`), and without it the cycle reads `unhealthy` /
    `params_update_not_seen`.
    """
    if str(change.get("kind")) == "text_slot":
        return emit("slot_update", "", {"messages": [], "slot": {
            "name": str(change.get("key")), "text": change.get("to")}},
            {"cycle_id": cid, "outcome": outcome,
             "target": str(change.get("target"))})
    u = params_update_for(change)
    return emit("mutate", "", {"system": {}, "params": u["params"]},
                {"cycle_id": cid, "outcome": outcome, "target": u["target"]})


def eval_order(cid, change, batch_min, wid):
    """The question to an evaluator (GH #927): one text change, and the batch
    size it has to be judged on. The texts travel in the BODY -- a prompt
    block runs to kilobytes, and the hop is what every edge on the way reads --
    while the hop names the order (`eval_tag`, the id of the `waits` row that
    remembers it) and nothing longer."""
    target = str(change.get("target") or "")
    return emit("eval", "", {"messages": [], "eval": {
        "cycle_id": cid, "target": target, "key": str(change.get("key") or ""),
        "from": change.get("from"), "to": change.get("to"),
        "batch_min": batch_min}},
        {"cycle_id": cid, "outcome": "eval_pending", "target": target,
         "eval_tag": wid})


def probe_order(cid, target):
    return emit("probe", "", {"messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                                            "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
                                            "text": json.dumps({
                                                "op": "probe",
                                                "cycle_id": cid,
                                                "target": target})}]},
                {"cycle_id": cid, "outcome": "applied"})


d = doc["body"]
header = (doc["envelope"].get("header") or {})
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
context = header.get("context") or {}

# A store answer carries `operation`; a colony mutation verdict carries
# `mutation`. Neither needs anything further from this cell.
#
# The third form is an ERROR echo, and it is the one GH #462 found: a target
# that refuses the params update answers this cell directly, and that answer
# carries a `finish_reason` and no turns at all. Without this line it fell
# through to the decide path, parsed `{}`, defaulted `action` to `none` and
# wrote a cycle row for a decision nobody took. The refusal is not silently
# lost -- it is a colony-wide error inside the probe's window, so the health
# check two hops later rules the cycle unhealthy and the revert plan is taken.
# What is NOT possible today is attributing it to its cycle: the answer is a
# fresh message with no context of ours, so this cell cannot know which change
# was refused. That is a substrate-shaped gap, not a script-shaped one.
#
# GH #927: ONE store answer is not an echo -- the read of a `waits` row that an
# evaluation verdict asked for. It is told apart by the phase this cell wrote
# on the read itself (`evalwait`), which comes back in the context; every
# write this cell makes goes out as `written`.
echo = "operation" in hop
resumed = echo and str(context.get("ar_phase") or "") == "evalwait"
if ((echo and not resumed) or "mutation" in d
        or str(hop.get("finish_reason") or "") == "error"):
    sys.stdout.write("[]")
    sys.exit(0)

stamp = now()

# The lane a message came in on (GH #927, review findings C1 and C2). Four
# edges lead into this cell, and the lane is what tells their messages apart:
# `revert` from the meter and the probe, `in_eval` from outside the hive, a
# store answer from ./receipts, and the judge's answer with no lane at all.
# The judge's edge asks for no lane, but a lane is not something a model can
# claim: it writes the TEXT of its tool call, and the hop is written by the
# cell that emits it. So each path below is taken on its lane and nowhere
# else -- the tool-call text alone must never open a path the judge is not
# allowed down.
route = str(hop.get("route") or "")

# ---- a verdict resumed: the wait it names came back from ./receipts ----
if resumed:
    rows = [r for r in rows_of(d) if isinstance(r, dict)]
    if str(hop.get("error_code") or "") or not rows:
        # A verdict whose wait is gone -- closed by the meter's next tick as
        # `eval_unanswered`, so the cycle already has its receipt -- or a read
        # that failed, which leaves the wait open for that same tick to close.
        # Either way the cycle is receipted exactly once, and acting here would
        # apply a change to a cycle that is already written down as discarded.
        sys.stdout.write("[]")
        sys.exit(0)
    w = rows[0]
    wid = str(w.get("id") or "")
    wc = as_obj(w.get("carry"))
    if str(w.get("kind") or "") != "eval" or not wc:
        sys.stdout.write("[]")
        sys.exit(0)
    ev = as_obj(as_obj(context.get("ar_carry")).get("eval"))
    cid = str(wc.get("cycle_id") or "")
    change = as_obj(wc.get("change"))
    goal_spec = as_obj(wc.get("ar_goal_spec"))
    # The bar is the one this cell set when it sent the order, read back from
    # its own wait row -- never from the answer, which could lower it.
    batch_min = int_or(wc.get("batch_min"), None)
    if batch_min is None:
        batch_min = batch_min_of(as_list(wc.get("ar_rules")), goal_spec)
    verdict, reason = evidence_ok(ev, goal_spec, batch_min)
    done = receipt("update", table="waits", set={"status": "done"},
                   where={"id": wid})
    if verdict != "apply":
        # Discarded is a recorded outcome, and the batch that failed is the
        # record: `evidence` keeps the whole answer, whatever it said.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([
            receipt("update", table="cycles",
                    set={"status": "closed", "outcome": "discarded",
                         "reason_code": reason, "evidence": ev},
                    where={"id": cid}),
            done]))
        sys.exit(0)
    # From here a text change is a change like any other: the wire, the
    # `applied` row the meter scans for, and the health check at once -- two
    # clocks, the probe's and the window's, as for a model or a number.
    #
    # `at` moves to NOW (review finding I2). The meter measures the effect
    # window from `cycles.at`, and until here it held the time the evaluation
    # was ORDERED -- traffic from before the text landed would be counted as
    # its effect. A model or a number is applied in the breath its row is
    # written, so for them the two times are one.
    #
    # No compare-and-set on `status: open` (review finding M3): if the meter
    # closed this cycle as `eval_unanswered` meanwhile, the text is leaving
    # anyway, and a row that says `discarded` over a colony running the text
    # would be the untruthful receipt. What happened wins: `applied`, and the
    # window and the probe measure it like any other change.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([
        change_message(change, cid, "applied"),
        receipt("update", table="cycles",
                set={"status": "applied", "outcome": "", "reason_code": "",
                     "evidence": ev, "at": stamp},
                where={"id": cid}),
        probe_order(cid, change.get("target")),
        done]))
    sys.exit(0)

# ---- a verdict arrived: an evaluation batch has ruled on a text change ----
#
# It names its order by `hop.eval_tag` and nothing else, so it is matched the
# way the meter matches an answer: one read of the `waits` row, with the
# verdict riding along in the carry. Asked for `status: open` on purpose -- a
# verdict that comes back after its wait was closed finds no row and is dropped
# without a word (GH #927).
#
# `in_eval` is the lane for a verdict and for NOTHING else (review finding
# C2). It is the hive's door from outside -- the colony around it passes the
# lane through from its own border -- so what arrives on it is somebody else's
# text. Read as a decision or a revert order it reached both other paths: a
# `slot_update` with any text at all, a model swap no judge had ruled on, and
# for a verdict that was a string a `no_action` row for a decision nobody took
# (the GH #462 class). Anything on this lane that is not a tagged verdict
# object is dropped without a row.
if route == "in_eval":
    ev = d.get("eval")
    tag = str(hop.get("eval_tag") or "")
    if not isinstance(ev, dict) or not tag:
        sys.stdout.write("[]")
        sys.exit(0)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt(
        "select", phase="evalwait",
        carry={"eval": {k: ev[k] for k in EVAL_KEYS if k in ev}},
        table="waits", columns=["id", "at", "kind", "carry", "status"],
        where={"id": tag, "status": "open"}, limit=1)]))
    sys.exit(0)

# The other half of the same rule: a verdict body on any other lane is no
# verdict. The lane is what makes one, not the shape of the body.
if "eval" in d:
    sys.stdout.write("[]")
    sys.exit(0)

msgs = d.get("messages") or []
call = {}
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("type") == "tool_call":
        call = m
if not call and msgs:
    call = msgs[-1]
try:
    a = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
except Exception:
    a = None
if not isinstance(a, dict):
    a = {}

# A `tool_call` turn off the wire carries the PROVIDER'S FUNCTION OBJECT
# verbatim -- `{"name": ..., "arguments": "<json string>"}`
# (`crates/meclaw-cells/src/llm/translate.rs`, `assistant_turn.push`) -- so the
# decision is one level in. A tool call authored inside this hive (the meter's
# and the probe's `revert`/`probe` orders) carries its arguments flat, because
# a `code` cell writes what it means.
#
# GH #462: both shapes have to be read here and only one ever was. Every test
# of this cell fed it the flat form on stdin, so the judge's real answer -- the
# only shape that ever reaches it in a running colony -- unwrapped to nothing,
# `action` defaulted to `none`, and the cycle closed as `no_action` over a
# colony where a model had in fact decided something. The loop had never once
# applied a change end to end.
if "name" in a and isinstance(a.get("arguments"), (str, dict)):
    a = as_obj(a.get("arguments"))

# ---- the revert path: the meter ruled that a change did not prove itself ----
#
# Taken on the lane `revert` and on no other (review finding C1). The edges
# `./meter -> ./mutator` and `./probe -> ./mutator` require it, and those two
# are the only cells that may order a way back: the plan they send is the one
# the cycle stored before its change was applied. The judge's edge carries no
# lane, and an `op: "revert"` in the judge's text used to be taken here anyway
# -- with no charter gate, no class and no evaluation, a direct `slot_update`
# of any text up to the colony's identity, or a model swap outside every step
# limit. It now ends on the decide path as `judge_cannot_revert`.
if route == "revert":
    if str(a.get("op") or "") != "revert":
        # Nothing but a revert order travels this lane; anything else on it
        # is nobody's, and a row for it would be a decision nobody took.
        sys.stdout.write("[]")
        sys.exit(0)
    cid = str(a.get("cycle_id") or "")
    plan = as_obj(a.get("plan"))
    if not plan:
        # No plan to take, so no revert happened -- and the row has to say that.
        # The meter closed it as `reverted` in the same breath as it ordered the
        # revert, so writing only a reason code here would leave a receipt
        # claiming a way back that was never taken, with the reason muttering
        # otherwise underneath. Same mechanic as the radius refusal below: the
        # cycle goes back to `applied`, which is what the colony actually is,
        # and the outcome names the refusal.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt(
            "update", table="cycles",
            set={"status": "applied", "outcome": "revert_refused",
                 "reason_code": "revert_plan_missing_at_revert_time"},
            where={"id": cid})]))
        sys.exit(0)
    # GH #927: the meter's revert order carries the charter's rules, and with
    # them the text half of the radius is asked on the way back too -- an
    # operator who took `text_slots` out of the radius while a text change was
    # standing gets `revert_refused`, like a key that left the numeric set. The
    # probe's revert carries none, and there the half is not asked: it comes
    # seconds after the change passed that radius, because the colony is
    # unhealthy NOW, and a health revert refused for want of a rules list would
    # keep a broken colony broken.
    rules = as_list(a.get("rules")) if "rules" in a else None
    # `from` is dropped before the check, and dropping it is the construction
    # the step limit is inert by: the limit judges the way THERE, and the way
    # back must not be re-judged by it. It is not symmetric -- 100 -> 60 is a
    # 40% step and passes, 60 -> 100 is a 67% step and would not -- so a plan
    # that happened to carry its own `from` would be refused for reversing a
    # change this loop itself allowed, leaving exactly the unproven value
    # standing that the revert exists to remove. The plan the judge is asked
    # for has no `from`, but the tool schema does not forbid one and this cell
    # replays what was stored.
    reason = check_change({k: v for k, v in plan.items() if k != "from"},
                          rules)
    if reason:
        # The stored plan does not pass the check the change itself had to
        # pass. It may be outside the radius as it stands NOW -- an operator
        # narrowed the key set while the window was open, or the row predates
        # the set -- or degenerate in its own right: no value, a relative
        # target, no target at all (GH #326). A way back that skips a bound the
        # way there had to pass is a second door, not a return.
        #
        # Nothing goes out, and the row is put back into the state it is
        # actually in: the change is still APPLIED, and the receipt says the
        # revert was refused and why.
        #
        # The meter has already closed this row as `reverted` by the time the
        # revert reaches this cell (it writes the verdict and the revert order in
        # the same breath), so leaving the row alone would leave a receipt
        # claiming a way back that never happened. Re-opening it is the honest
        # move and it is also the loud one: `status: applied` is exactly what the
        # meter scans for, so the cycle stays the open one and the loop starts
        # nothing new until a human resolves it.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt(
            "update", table="cycles",
            set={"status": "applied", "outcome": "revert_refused",
                 "reason_code": reason},
            where={"id": cid})]))
        sys.exit(0)
    # The way back travels the same wire the change travelled, because a revert
    # that took a different path would be a second mechanism to trust.
    out = [change_message(plan, cid, "reverted")]
    out.append(receipt("update", table="cycles",
                       set={"status": "closed", "outcome": "reverted"},
                       where={"id": cid}))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)

# ---- the decide path: the judge has ruled ----
cid = str(a.get("cycle_id") or context.get("ar_cycle") or "")
goal = str(context.get("ar_goal") or "")
action = str(a.get("action") or "none")
change = as_obj(a.get("change"))
plan = as_obj(a.get("revert_plan"))
require_plan = str(context.get("ar_require_plan") or "1") != "0"
judged = {"action": action, "reasoning": str(a.get("reasoning") or "")}
simulated = as_obj(a.get("simulated"))
measured = as_obj(context.get("ar_measured"))
# What the meter showed the judge for this cycle (GH #927): the rule rows, the
# goal row, and the ids of the hints it handed over. Absent on a hop from an
# older meter, which reads as no rules -- the closed defaults -- and no goal.
rules = [r for r in as_list(context.get("ar_rules")) if isinstance(r, dict)]
goal_spec = as_obj(context.get("ar_goal_spec"))
hints = as_list(context.get("ar_hints"))
source = str(goal_spec.get("source") or "")

# `role`, `hints` and `evidence` are on EVERY row this path writes, empty where
# they mean nothing, so a column is never sometimes missing (GH #927).
base_row = {"id": cid or ("cycle:" + uuid.uuid4().hex), "goal": goal, "at": stamp,
            "measured": measured, "judged": judged, "simulated": simulated,
            "change": change, "revert_plan": plan, "verified": {}, "effect": {},
            "role": "" if source in ("", "colony") else source,
            "hints": hints, "evidence": {}}

if str(a.get("op") or "") == "revert":
    # The judge answered with a revert order (review finding C1). A way back is
    # the meter's or the probe's to order, on their lane, from the plan stored
    # before the change; the judge's word for one is a change like any other
    # and has not passed a single check. Refused, with the receipt as the only
    # emission. The row is THIS cycle's (`ar_cycle`, the meter's id for it):
    # the id in the order names the cycle it wanted reverted, and a row under
    # that id would collide with that cycle's own.
    row = dict(base_row,
               id=str(context.get("ar_cycle") or "") or
               ("cycle:" + uuid.uuid4().hex),
               judged=dict(judged, action="revert"), status="closed",
               outcome="refused", reason_code="judge_cannot_revert")
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt("insert", table="cycles", row=row)]))
    sys.exit(0)

if str(change.get("kind") or "") == "text_slot":
    # The charter's gate comes before the judge's `action` (review finding
    # I3). A text in a `never` class is refused whatever the judge called its
    # answer, and a text in an owner-only class is the owner's proposal under
    # `owner_approval_required` whether the judge said `change`, `propose` or
    # `none` -- one receipt, nothing else leaves.
    gate = charter_gate(change, rules)
    if gate:
        row = dict(base_row, status="closed", outcome=gate[0],
                   reason_code=gate[1])
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt("insert", table="cycles",
                                             row=row)]))
        sys.exit(0)

if action != "change":
    # `propose` and `none` both end the cycle here, and they are recorded
    # differently on purpose: a proposal is a message to a human, and a human
    # who cannot find it later has not been sent one.
    row = dict(base_row, status="closed",
               outcome="proposed" if action == "propose" else "no_action",
               reason_code="judge_" + action)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt("insert", table="cycles", row=row)]))
    sys.exit(0)

if str(change.get("kind") or "") == "text_slot":
    # A text change never goes the model's way (GH #927). It is classified
    # before anything else is looked at, re-checked with its plan, and then
    # ASKED about rather than applied: the change leaves as an evaluation
    # order, and the cycle stays `open` as `eval_pending` until the verdict
    # comes back on `in_eval` -- or the meter's next tick closes it as
    # `eval_unanswered`.
    status, reason = classify_slot(change, rules)
    if status == "eval":
        reason = revert_ok_text(change, plan, require_plan)
        status = "refused" if reason else "eval"
    if status != "eval":
        # Refused or proposed, the receipt is the ONLY emission: no order to an
        # evaluator, no text anywhere near a cell.
        row = dict(base_row, status="closed", outcome=status,
                   reason_code=reason)
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt("insert", table="cycles",
                                             row=row)]))
        sys.exit(0)
    wid = "wait:" + uuid.uuid4().hex
    batch_min = batch_min_of(rules, goal_spec)
    # The wait row goes out first, so it is in the store before any verdict
    # can ask for it. It remembers everything the resumption needs -- the
    # verdict comes back as a fresh message with no context of ours.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([
        receipt("insert", table="waits", row={
            "id": wid, "at": stamp, "kind": "eval", "status": "open",
            "carry": {"cycle_id": base_row["id"], "change": change,
                      "revert_plan": plan, "ar_goal_spec": goal_spec,
                      "ar_rules": rules, "batch_min": batch_min}}),
        receipt("insert", table="cycles",
                row=dict(base_row, status="open", outcome="eval_pending",
                         reason_code="")),
        eval_order(base_row["id"], change, batch_min, wid)]))
    sys.exit(0)

reason = check(change, plan, require_plan)
if reason:
    # The judge asked for something the charter does not allow. This is the
    # normal case for a model in a control loop, not an exception -- which is
    # why the refusal is a recorded outcome rather than an error.
    row = dict(base_row, status="closed", outcome="refused", reason_code=reason)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([receipt("insert", table="cycles", row=row)]))
    sys.exit(0)

out = [
    change_message(change, base_row["id"], "applied"),
    receipt("insert", table="cycles",
            row=dict(base_row, status="applied", outcome="", reason_code="")),
    # The health check runs immediately, not on the next tick: a colony that
    # was broken by a mutation must not stay broken for a measurement window.
    probe_order(base_row["id"], change.get("target")),
]
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))

max_numeric_step_pct.description: How far one cycle may move a numeric param, in percent. A cap that jumps by an order of magnitude is not a tuning step; the limit keeps one cycle's mistake small enough that the next cycle can measure its way out.

numeric_param_keys.description: The numeric half of the radius, as a key set. This cell cannot see a target's cell type, and whether a params update lands is a fact about that type: only the types with a params lane merge one, and a `code` cell has none. The default is the `llm` cell's runtime-mutable numeric params, because that is the cell type the radius is about. A key outside the set is refused with `key_outside_radius_<key>` rather than receipted as applied -- in BOTH directions: a stored revert plan whose key has since left the set closes as `revert_refused` with the change still standing, never as `reverted`. A JSON array here; a comma-separated string is read the same way, because an override reaches this knob as a config line somebody types.

description.purpose: The cell that turns a decision into a change -- and the cell that refuses one. Every claim the judge made is re-checked deterministically: the radius (model, numeric params, and the text slot classes the charter lists -- identity never, the owner's classes only as a proposal), the revert plan (present, well formed, and actually the inverse; byte for byte for a text), the step size. A model or a number that passes leaves as an ordinary params update addressed to the one cell it names -- body `{system:{}, params:{...}}`, hop.target naming the cell -- which the target merges into its live params and answers with nothing at all. A text change is asked about before it is made: it leaves as an `eval` order, and only a batch of at least `max(eval_min_batch, min_samples)` that passes and moves the goal's metric past its floor lets it out as a `slot_update` -- body `{messages: [], slot: {name, text}}`, same hop -- while anything less closes the cycle as `discarded` with the batch as its evidence (GH #927).
description.use_when: One per argus hive, downstream of ./judge, of ./meter's revert lane and of the hive's `in_eval` lane.
description.not_in_scope: No operator lane, and there must not be one: a control loop that can override the gates it runs under is not governed, it is merely polite. No topology change either -- a judge that asks for one gets `outside_radius` and a receipt saying so. And no mutation: since GH #304 nothing here authors a diff, so the loop cannot add, remove or rewire a cell even if somebody drew it an edge to /colony/mutations. Nor can it move a param on a cell type that has no params lane -- a `code` cell's numeric cap is out of radius today and comes back as `key_outside_radius_<key>`, because a receipt that says `applied` over a colony where nothing moved is the same defect wearing the other half of the radius. The radius binds the way BACK as well: a revert plan outside it is refused as `revert_refused` and the cycle stays open, because a way back nobody took must not read as taken. Nor does a text change land on the judge's word alone: no passing evaluation, no `slot_update` -- and a text the charter keeps from this loop (`never`, `owner_only`) leaves no message at all, only its receipt.
